newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos dispels health doubts.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos dispels health doubts.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday he was in good health and that jitters in the Manila stock market over his spell in hospital at the weekend appeared to be over.
"If it were only up to me, I would go there and hold my office in the stock market to show them how healthy I am," Ramos said at his weekly news conference.

Ramos, 68, spent the weekend in hospital after complaining of pains in his joints on Thursday. Doctors said he was suffering from a throat infection and was otherwise in good health, although he needed to slow down.
There was little immediate reaction to his illness in the markets, although some newspapers reported he may have suffered a minor stroke. Both Ramos and his doctors denied the reports.

"Early this week, he made several public appearances and most people have seen that he was doing well," said Fitzgerald Aclan, head of research at Dharamala Securities. "Right now, the concern has died down."
Ramos told reporters that although the stock market had fallen on Monday and Tuesday, perhaps on rumours over his health, it had now recovered.
"This morning, after seeing me on the job for 10 hours yesterday, the stock market recovered," he said.
The Philippines composite index closed 0.41 percent up at 3,105.80 points on Wednesday.
Ramos looked in good health during the news conference. He spoke steadily, showing no signs of any throat trouble, and occasionally burst into chuckles.

He said he had no plans to cut down on his appointments despite the advice of doctors that he should do so. But newspapers have said he appears to have slowed down somewhat, cancelling several trips around the country.
Asked whether his illness had affected his pace of work, Ramos said: "It will remain the same."
